catalog_quote: [pp. 59-60, sec. 1.2.3.3 Distributed prominence] While it is superficially clear that Phuthi lacks stressed syllables, if stress is phonological prominence realised by some phonetic complex of pitch/loudness/duration, Phuthi will be seen to reflect word-prominence with a nuanced (in part, paradigm-specific) interaction of tone and voice settings reflecting partial metrical properties (e.g. a right-aligned trochee). ... the general phrasal target for rightwards H tone realignment in non-grammatical paradigms (e.g. the indicative) is the antepenult; phrase-medially the target is the penult syllable. [p. 256, sec. 4.1.4.6] All Phuthi (and other Nguni) phrase-penult syllables are redundantly long ... I propose, therefore, that the penult itself is identified as the heavy left element (head) of a single, right-aligned, binary stress foot, that is a syllabic trochee in the Hayes (1995) typology [p. 257] ... identify the penult as the stressed position (49-50) and then make that metrically strong position (the foothead) heavy, by the SWP (51). [p. 761, sec. 8.2.2] We will conclude by saying that stress in Phuthi amounts to the cumulative set of align and anti-align conditions that require reference to the antepenult-penult boundary (and also in part to the penult-ultima and ultima-edge boundaries). [p. 762, sec. 8.2.2.1] phrase-final words redundantly lengthen their penult syllable. This is true for all phrases in Phuthi.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Genus-level statement covering Phuthi (S404) with the rest of Zone S: stress, realised as lengthening, falls on the penultimate syllable of the phrase/sentence (hence of a word in citation/phrase-final position) in declaratives; suspended in questions and exclamations. No Phuthi-specific primary statement was obtainable.
new_statements.exceptions: Lozi excluded; accent not used in interrogative and exclamatory sentences.
new_statements.domain_note: Explicitly phrase/sentence-level penultimate length-stress (demarcative, end of declarative phrase); word-level stress not separately described. Statement is a survey generalisation for Zone S, not a first-hand description of Phuthi.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources refer to Phuthi/siPhuthi (Guthrie S404, glottocode phut1246), spoken mainly in southern Lesotho (Donnelly's fieldwork: Sigxodo and Mpapa) and adjacent Eastern Cape; Bourquin 1927 describes the Tinana-river (East Griqualand border) community. The quoted stress statement is NOT Phuthi-specific: it is Gowlett's generalisation over all Guthrie Zone S languages except Lozi.

sources.note: Zone-S-wide generalisation (Phuthi included as S404): all Zone S languages except Lozi have a penultimate length-stress feature signalling the end of a phrase/sentence in declaratives; not used in interrogatives/exclamatives. Nothing Phuthi-specific on stress (the Phuthi-specific material is vowel inventory and vowel harmony, citing Donnelly 1996).
